ja: 弟が転職するって言ってたよ。
en: My brother said he was changing jobs.
alternatives: My brother told me he was changing jobs.
My brother said he was switching jobs.
point: said の後は時制を一つ過去にずらす（is→was）

ja: 引っ越すことにしたんだ。
en: I decided to move.
alternatives: I've decided to move.
I decided to move out.
point: 「〜することにした」は decide to do

ja: また連絡してね。
en: Keep in touch.
alternatives: Stay in touch.
Let's keep in touch.
point: 「連絡を取り合う」は keep in touch

ja: 最近、何にハマってるの？
en: What are you into lately?
alternatives: What have you been into lately?
What are you into these days?
point: 「ハマってる」は be into ～

ja: 忙しいけど、元気にやってるよ。
en: Although I'm busy, I'm doing well.
alternatives: Even though I'm busy, I'm doing fine.
I'm doing well, even though I'm busy.
point: although の後ろも文の形。but とは重ねない

ja: 最近、ジムに全然行けてない。
en: I haven't been to the gym lately.
alternatives: I haven't gone to the gym at all lately.
I haven't made it to the gym lately.
point: lately とは現在完了を使う

ja: 私が独立してなければ今も周囲に従う。
en: Without going independent, I'd still toe the line.
alternatives: I'd still conform if I hadn't gone independent.
Without becoming independent, I'd still conform to others.
point: 独立しなかった過去の仮定と、今も周囲に従う結果を結ぶ。

ja: 君が慣れたら私が訪ねるよ。
en: I'll visit once you've settled in.
alternatives: I'll come by once you've settled in.
I'll visit after you've adjusted.
point: settle in は新しい環境に慣れて落ち着く。

ja: 残っていたら、今ごろ結婚してたかも。
en: If I'd stayed, I might be married now.
alternatives: If I had stayed, I might be married by now.
Had I stayed, I might be married now.
point: 過去の仮定 + 今の結果は if I'd + might be

ja: また連絡してね。
en: Keep in touch.
alternatives: Stay in touch.
Keep in touch, okay?
point: 「連絡を保つ」は keep in touch

ja: 前に話してた仕事、決まったよ。
en: The job I mentioned came through.
alternatives: I got the job I mentioned.
I landed the job I told you about.
point: come through は「うまく決まる」

ja: 近々、会わないとね。
en: We should get together soon.
alternatives: We need to meet up soon.
We have to get together soon.
point: 「会う」は get together / meet up

ja: 忙しくなきゃもっと電話するのに。
en: If I weren't swamped, I'd call more.
alternatives: I'd call more if I weren't swamped.
If I weren't busy, I'd call more.
point: 現在の仮定は were。swamped は忙殺されている

ja: 彼女は私の平気なふりを見抜いたと言った。
en: She said she'd seen through my calm facade.
alternatives: She said she'd spotted my pretense of calm.
She said my calmness hadn't fooled her.
point: seen through my calm facade は私の平気なふりを見抜いたことを表す。

ja: こんなに忙しいのは初めてだよ。
en: Never have I been this busy.
alternatives: I've never been this busy.
This is the busiest I've ever been.
point: Never を文頭に出すと have I been の語順になる

ja: 今、何してるの？
en: What are you doing?
alternatives: What are you up to?
What are you doing now?
point: 今していることは現在進行形で聞く

ja: 私は最近、人脈を作り直してる。
en: I've been rebuilding my network lately.
alternatives: I've been rebuilding my connections recently.
I've been reestablishing my contacts lately.
point: rebuild my network は人とのつながりを築き直す。

ja: 私、家を買ったよ。
en: I bought a house.
alternatives: I purchased a house.
I bought my own house.
point: bought は buy の過去形。

ja: 最近どうしてたか教えて。
en: Tell me how you've been.
alternatives: Let me know how you've been.
Tell me what you've been up to.
point: how の後ろは疑問文の語順にしない

ja: 私が面子に固執しなければ謝れたのに。
en: Had I swallowed my pride, I could've apologized.
alternatives: If I'd swallowed my pride, I could've said sorry.
I could've apologized had I set my pride aside.
point: swallow my pride は面子を捨てて行動する。

ja: 私が辛かったのは努力を無視されたことだ。
en: What stung was having my efforts brushed aside.
alternatives: It was the dismissal of my efforts that hurt.
What hurt was having my hard work disregarded.
point: what stung で心に刺さった出来事を際立たせる。

ja: 私が選べるなら過去を水に流すのに。
en: Were it my call, I'd let bygones be bygones.
alternatives: If I could choose, I'd leave the past behind.
If it were my choice, I'd forget past grievances.
point: let bygones be bygones は過去のわだかまりを水に流す。

ja: 母は私に引き継ぎを頼んだ。
en: Mom asked me to take over.
alternatives: Mom asked me to assume control.
Mom asked me to take charge.
point: take over は責任や仕事を引き継ぐ。

ja: どうやって成し遂げたのか教えてよ。
en: Tell me how you pulled it off.
alternatives: I'm curious how you pulled it off.
I want to know how you pulled it off.
point: how の後ろは平叙の語順(you pulled)

ja: 母は私に言いたくないことを認めさせた。
en: Mom made me admit what I'd rather conceal.
alternatives: Mom made me admit something I'd rather hide.
Mom forced an admission I'd rather have avoided.
point: would rather leave unsaid は口にせずにおきたいという含み。

ja: 私は異動で脇に追いやられた。
en: I was sidelined by the transfer.
alternatives: The transfer pushed me to the sidelines.
I was marginalized through the transfer.
point: sidelined は中心的な仕事や役割から外される。

ja: 私は親切に見せた干渉を見抜けばな。
en: I wish I'd recognized that kindness as meddling.
alternatives: I wish I'd seen that kindness was really meddling.
If only I'd realized that kindness was unwanted interference.
point: meddling は親切に見せても望まれていない干渉を指す。

ja: その頃は大変だったでしょうね。
en: That must have been hard back then.
alternatives: It must have been tough back then.
Things must have been hard back then.
point: 過去の推量は must have + 過去分詞

ja: 君、少し痩せた気がするんだけど。
en: You seem to have lost some weight.
alternatives: You look like you've lost some weight.
I feel like you've lost a little weight.
point: seem to で断定を避けて柔らかく伝える

ja: 私は今話せるよ。
en: I can talk now.
alternatives: I can chat now.
I'm free to talk now.
point: can で今話せる状況を伝える。

ja: 今、猫を飼ってるよ。
en: I have a cat.
alternatives: I've got a cat.
I have a pet cat.
point: 数えられる名詞には a を付ける

ja: 最近、仕事はどう？
en: How's work these days?
alternatives: How's work going?
How is work lately?
point: 調子を聞くときは How で始める

ja: その頃には私は就職してた。
en: I'd landed a job by then.
alternatives: I'd found a job by then.
I'd secured a job by that point.
point: land a job は仕事を得る。

ja: 私の成功は君には受け入れ難かったかも。
en: My success might've been a bitter pill for you.
alternatives: You may have struggled to accept my success.
You might've found my success hard to swallow.
point: a bitter pill は受け入れるのが苦しい出来事。

ja: 私、犬を飼うよ。
en: I'll get a dog.
alternatives: I'm going to get a dog.
I'm getting a dog.
point: will でこれからの予定を話す。

ja: 燃え尽きて、のんびりやってる。
en: Burned out, I'm taking it easy.
alternatives: Having burned out, I'm taking it easy.
Having burned out, I've been relaxing lately.
point: Having + 過去分詞で先に起きた理由を示す

ja: 今は10キロ走れるんだ。
en: I can run 10K now.
alternatives: I can run 10 kilometers now.
These days I can run 10K.
point: 今できることは can

ja: 今はここに住んでる。
en: I live here now.
alternatives: I'm living here now.
Now I live here.
point: 住んでいる状態は現在形 live

ja: 私の転職は手放しで成功とは言えない。
en: I can't call my job change an unqualified success.
alternatives: My job change wasn't a complete success.
Calling my job change wholly successful would be misleading.
point: unqualified success は留保のない全面的な成功。転職は job change。

ja: 驚いたのは、彼女が辞めてたこと。
en: What floored me was that she'd quit.
alternatives: What surprised me was that she'd quit.
What shocked me was that she'd quit.
point: What ～ was that で強調。floor は仰天させる

ja: 私はまだ峠を越えたとは言えない。
en: I wouldn't say I'm out of the woods.
alternatives: I wouldn't say I'm in the clear.
I can't say my troubles are over.
point: out of the woods は危険や問題を脱した状態。

ja: 残ってたら、今ごろ課長だよ。
en: If I'd stayed, I'd be manager now.
alternatives: I'd be manager now if I'd stayed.
If I'd stayed on, I'd be manager by now.
point: 過去の条件は had + 過去分詞、今の結果は would + 原形

ja: 新しい子犬がいるよ。
en: There's a new puppy.
alternatives: We have a new puppy.
I have a new puppy.
point: There's の後の名詞が新情報。a を忘れない

ja: あの旅行がなければ燃え尽きてた。
en: Without that trip, I'd have burned out.
alternatives: I'd have burned out without that trip.
But for that trip, I'd have burned out.
point: 「〜がなければ」の過去の話は would have + 過去分詞

ja: 最後に会ったの、去年の夏？
en: Haven't seen you since last summer?
alternatives: We haven't met since last summer, right?
Was the last time last summer?
Last time we met was last summer, right?
point: since で起点を言うなら現在完了

ja: 京都にいる弟は、元気だよ。
en: My brother in Kyoto is fine.
alternatives: My brother in Kyoto is doing well.
My brother who's in Kyoto is doing fine.
point: 名詞の後ろに in Kyoto を置いて説明する

ja: 音沙汰なくて、最悪を覚悟してた。
en: Hearing nothing, I feared the worst.
alternatives: Not hearing from you, I feared the worst.
When I heard nothing, I feared the worst.
point: 否定の分詞構文は Not hearing

ja: 子どもに振り回されっぱなしだよ。
en: The kids have me running around nonstop.
alternatives: My kids have me running around all the time.
The kids keep me running around nonstop.
point: have + 人 + -ing で「〜させられている」感じ

ja: ちょっと聞いてもいい？
en: Can I ask you something?
alternatives: Could I ask you something?
Can I ask you a question?
point: 許可は Can I ～? で軽く聞ける

ja: まさか君がベルリンに落ち着くとはね。
en: Who'd have thought you'd end up in Berlin?
alternatives: Who would have imagined you'd end up in Berlin?
Who'd have guessed you'd end up in Berlin?
point: Who'd have thought 〜? は「誰が思っただろう」

ja: 私たちは早く仲直りすればよかった。
en: I wish we'd buried the hatchet sooner.
alternatives: I wish we'd made peace sooner.
If only we'd settled our differences sooner.
point: bury the hatchet はけんかを終わりにして仲直りすること。

ja: 昇進したの君だって噂だよ。
en: Word is you're the one who got promoted.
alternatives: Word has it you're the one who got promoted.
I hear you're the one who got promoted.
point: Word is 〜 は「噂では」。that は省ける

ja: 傍目には成功でも私は達成感が薄い。
en: Though seemingly successful, I feel little fulfillment.
alternatives: Though I seem successful, I feel scarcely fulfilled.
I feel little satisfaction despite appearing successful.
point: fulfillment は自分の生き方や達成に満足する感覚。

ja: 私は今歩いてる。
en: I'm walking now.
alternatives: I'm walking right now.
I'm walking at the moment.
point: 今進んでいる動作は am + walking。

ja: 新しい友達が数人いる。
en: I've got new friends.
alternatives: I have new friends.
I've made some new friends.
point: 複数の友達には friends を使う。

ja: 前よりずっと元気そうだね。
en: You look much better than before.
alternatives: You look way better than last time.
You look a lot better than before.
point: 比較を強めるのは much / a lot / way

ja: 私が耐えた失望は今は距離感になった。
en: The disillusionment I endured has since become detachment.
alternatives: The disappointment I lived through has become emotional distance.
My earlier disillusionment has now turned into detachment.
point: disillusionment は理想が崩れた失望、detachment は心の距離。

ja: 何か変わったことある？
en: Is there anything new with you?
alternatives: Has anything new happened lately?
Is anything new going on with you?
point: 疑問文の「何か」は anything

ja: 元気でよかった。
en: I'm glad you're doing well.
alternatives: I'm happy you're doing well.
It's good to hear you're doing well.
point: glad の後ろの that は省略できる

ja: 写真を見てもいい？
en: Can I see photos?
alternatives: Could I look at the photos?
Can you show me the photos?
point: Can I で許可を求める。

ja: 誘ってくれていれば、行ったのに。
en: If you'd invited me, I'd have gone.
alternatives: I'd have gone if you'd invited me.
Had you invited me, I would have gone.
point: 過去の仮定は had + 過去分詞、結果は would have + 過去分詞

ja: 会社のそばの店、閉店したよ。
en: The shop by my office closed.
alternatives: The store near my office closed down.
The place near my office has closed.
point: 名詞のすぐ後ろに前置詞句で場所を足す

ja: 最近ジョギングを始めた。
en: I started jogging recently.
alternatives: I recently started jogging.
I've taken up jogging lately.
point: start のあとは ～ing でも to でもよい

ja: 私は最近、家を探してる。
en: I've been house hunting lately.
alternatives: I've been looking for a home lately.
I've been searching for a house recently.
point: have been hunting で最近続けている家探し。
